newsitem.title: UK: Olivetti may see operating profits this yr.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti may see operating profits this yr.

text.p: Troubled Italian high-tech group Olivetti said on Friday that it might break into the black at the operating level by the end of the year.
A company spokesman told analysts in London: "The company has the opportunity to recover profitability at the operating level from now to the year-end."
Company executives also said that Olivetti expects net debt to be around 2.0 trillion lire by the of 1996, down from a figure of 2.4 trillion at the end of August.
But they added that the sales Olivetti had lost through recent instability were unlikely to be recovered by the end of the year.

Chief executive Roberto Colaninno said the company was in talks to sell its loss-making personal computer business as part of the group's plans to raise between 1.0 and 1.2 trillion lire from asset disposals in 1996 and 1997.
"We need to sell this company before the end of the year," he said. He did not indentify any discussion partners

Colaninno has said that Olivetti plans to sell off its Tecnost bank cash dispenser business, computer mainframe maintenance services group Decision Systems International and its Venture Capital USA unit along with the PC business.
He told analysts in Milan on Thursday that the group's future lay in its telecommunications interests.
